Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:10:1.english: Both something that is not fitting for it - [Such as when it] licked his plowed field and scorched his stones.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:10:2.hebrew: ואילו שהאש משלמת שלא בכוונה - דליכא דרבה מיניה, דמים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:10:2.english: But [that] fire pays [when ignited] unintentionally - where there is no [punishment] greater than it, [one pays] monetary value.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:10:3.hebrew: מה שאין כן בבור - דפטר ביה מיתת אדם, דכתיב "שור" ולא אדם — לא קתני:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:10:3.english: Which is not the case with a pit - for [Scripture] exempts the death of a person in it, as it is written: "an ox" — [and] not a person — [this, the baraita] does not teach.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:12:1.hebrew: אלא רבא גופיה - הא דאותיב לעיל "אשו שלא בכוונה", לאו דפשיטא ליה דלא משלם ובתיובתא מייתי לה, אלא בלשון בעיא אייתי לה. והכי קאמר ליה רבא לרבה: אי הכי, דשור שלא בכוונה שאין כופר יש דמים, אשו שלא בכוונה מאי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:12:1.english: Rather, Rava himself - That which he raised above [regarding] "his fire [that killed] unintentionally," [it was] not that it was obvious to him that he does not pay and he brought it as a refutation; rather, he brought it in the form of a dilemma. And this is what Rava was saying to Rabbah: If so, that [in the case of] an ox [that killed] unintentionally, where there is no ransom, there is [payment of] value, what [is the law regarding] his fire [that killed] unintentionally?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:13:1.hebrew: אבל אש דבכוונה לא משלם כופר - חדא דאין כופר באש, ועוד דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:13:1.english: But [with regard to] fire, where [if it was done] intentionally he does not pay ransom - First, because there is no ransom for fire; and furthermore, because he incurs the greater [penalty].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:15:1.hebrew: לרבות כופר שלא בכוונה - אע"ג דאין השור בסקילה, ופליגא אדרבה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:15:1.english: To include ransom [where the ox killed] unintentionally - Even though the ox is not [subject to] stoning, and [this] disagrees with Rabba.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:16:1.english: To include a slave [killed] unintentionally - For the fine.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:1:1.hebrew: מיהו בן חורין - דאשכחן ביה כופר ע"פ עצמו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:1:1.english: However, a freeman - Where we find regarding him [liability for] ransom based on his own [admission].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:1:2.hebrew: והיכי דמי כגון דאתו סהדי כו' - דהכא ודאי משלם כופר, דכופרא כפרה ולא קנסא דליפטר משום הודאת עצמו. והיכא דליכא עדים כלל, הוא דפטרנא מכופר משום גזירת הכתוב, דאין השור בסקילה; והכא הרי השור בסקילה בהעדאת העדים, דאי נמי תם הוי — בר סקילה הוא. הלכך, היכא דליכא עדים כלל, דאינו בר כופר, משלם דמים. אבל עבד, דלא משכחת ביה קנס ע"פ עצמו — דאי נמי אתו סהדי ואמרי קטל עבד, ולא ידעינן אי תם אי מועד, ואמר מריה מועד הוא, דפטור מקנס, אע"ג דהשור בסקילה, ואפילו תם, כדאמרינן לקמן: כל שחייב מיתה בבן חורין חייב בעבד, מיהו מודה בקנס פטור — הלכך כי ליכא עדים כלל, אפילו דמים לא משלם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:1:2.english: And what are the circumstances? Such as where witnesses came, etc. - For here [the owner] certainly pays ransom, since ransom is atonement and not a fine such that he should be exempt due to his own admission. And it is [only] where there are no witnesses at all that we exempt [him] from ransom due to the scriptural decree, because the ox is not subject to stoning; whereas here, behold, the ox is subject to stoning through the testimony of the witnesses, for even if it were an innocuous [ox], it is subject to stoning. Therefore, where there are no witnesses at all, where he is not subject to ransom, he pays [the victim's] monetary value. But [in the case of] a slave, where you do not find a fine [imposed] based on his own admission — for even if witnesses come and say, "It killed a slave," and we do not know whether [it was] innocuous or forewarned, and its owner says, "It is forewarned," he is exempt from the fine, even though the ox is subject to stoning, and even [if it is] innocuous, as we say below, "Whoever is liable to death for [killing] a freeman is liable for [killing] a slave," nevertheless, one who admits to a fine is exempt — therefore, when there are no witnesses at all, he does not even pay [the slave's] monetary value.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:21:1.hebrew: אם כופר כתיב במקום תשלומים - דסברא דלרבויי אחריני אתא לתשלומין, דלגופיה לא אצטריך, דהוה ליה למכתב כופר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:21:1.english: “If a ransom” is written in the place of payment - For [it is] logical that it comes to include others for payment, since for itself it was not needed, as [the verse] should have written “a ransom.”

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:21:2.hebrew: אם עבד לא כתיב גבי תשלומין - אלא גבי נגיחה, "אם עבד יגח", ולגופיה אצטריך לחלק בין עבד לבן חורין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:21:2.english: “If a slave” is not written regarding payment - Rather, [it is written] regarding the goring: “If [an ox] gores a slave,” and it is needed for itself, to distinguish between a slave and a freeman.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:22:1.english: To render liable for minors - [to] stoning.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:23:1.english: And is it not a logical inference - and a verse is not needed.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:23:2.english: Since [Scripture] rendered liable - [to] death, in [the case of] a person who kills a person.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:23:3.english: And [it is] liable - [to] death, [in the case of] an ox [that kills] a person.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:23:4.hebrew: לא חלקת בין נהרגים קטנים לגדולים - דכתיב "כי יכה כל נפש אדם", אפילו קטנים במשמע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:23:4.english: You did not distinguish between minors and adults who are killed - For it is written, "[If a man] strikes any human life" — even minors are implied.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:24:1.hebrew: מה אדם באדם שלא עשה כו' - רוצח קטן כגדול, דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ד:י״ז) "ואיש כי יכה" — איש ולא קטן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:24:1.english: If [in the case of] a person [killing] a person [it] did not render, etc. - [That is, it did not render] a minor [who is a] murderer like an adult, as it is written (Leviticus 24:17): "And a man who strikes" — a man, and not a minor.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:24:2.english: It renders [one] liable in it - For those who are killed, minors just as adults.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:4:1.hebrew: אלא לאו דמים - וקתני כל שחייב בבן חורין חייב בעבד, וכיון דאמרת בן חורין ע"פ עצמו משלם דמים, אמאי קתני לגבי עבד אינו משלם ע"פ עצמו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:4:1.english: Rather, is it not [referring to] value - And [the baraita] teaches: "Whatever one is liable for in [the case of] a freeman, one is liable for in [the case of] a slave." And since you say [that for] a freeman he pays [the victim's] value on his own admission, why does it teach regarding a slave [that] he does not pay on his own admission?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:5:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר כל שחייב כו' - הכי פירושא דברייתא דקתני כל — לאו במודה מפי עצמו קאי, אלא בהעדאת עדים, כסתם כל באי לב"ד. והעדאת עדים — ליכא מידי דמחייבת בבן חורין דלא מיחייב בעבד. והכי קאמר: כל שחייב בבן חורין בכוונה ע"פ עדים כופר — כלומר, כל שחייב בבן חורין כופר, כגון בכוונה וע"פ עדים — חייב נמי בעבד בכוונה ע"פ עדים קנס שלשים, דהא השור בסקילה. וכל שחייב בבן חורין דמים — והיכי דמי? כגון שלא בכוונה ע"פ עדים — חייב נמי בעבד דמים. אבל ע"פ עצמו, אע"ג דבבן חורין משלם דמים, בעבד פטור, כדאמרן, הואיל ומצינו חילוק בע"פ עצמו בין כופר דבן חורין לקנס דעבד. אבל בעדים שלא בכוונה לא אשכחן חומרא בכופר מבקנס, דהכא והכא פטור; הלכך לגבי דמים תרוייהו כי הדדי נינהו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:5:1.english: This is what it is saying: Any [case] where one is liable, etc. - This is the explanation of the baraita that teaches "any": it does not refer to one who admits from his own mouth, rather to the testimony of witnesses, like the ordinary [case of] all who come to court. And [with] the testimony of witnesses, there is nothing for which you obligate [him] in [the case of] a freeman that he is not obligated in [the case of] a slave. And this is what it is saying: Any [case] where one is liable for a freeman, intentionally, based on witnesses, [to pay] ransom — that is, any [case] where one is liable for a freeman [to pay] ransom, such as intentionally and based on witnesses — he is also liable for a slave, intentionally, based on witnesses, [to pay] the fine of thirty [shekels], since the ox is [subject] to stoning. And any [case] where one is liable for a freeman [to pay] the value — and what is the case? Such as unintentionally, based on witnesses — he is also liable for a slave [to pay] the value. However, based on his own mouth, even though for a freeman he pays the value, for a slave he is exempt, as we said, since we found a distinction in [the case of] his own mouth between the ransom for a freeman and the fine for a slave. However, with witnesses [where the goring was] unintentional, we do not find greater stringency in ransom than in the fine, for both here and there he is exempt; therefore, regarding the value, both of them are alike.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:6:1.hebrew: אי הכי - דשורו שלא בכוונה ע"פ עדים, דליתיה בתורת כופר, משלם דמים — כיון שיש דמים למיתת אדם במקום שאין כופר וקנס — אשו נמי, דליתיה בתורת כופר, לשלם דמים שלא בכוונה, דהא ישנה בתורת נזקין. ומיהו בכוונה, פשיטא לן דפטור, דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:6:1.english: If that is so - that [in the case of] his ox [killing] unintentionally based on [the testimony of] witnesses, which is not subject to the law of ransom, he pays [the victim's] monetary value — since there is [liability for] monetary value for the death of a person where there is no ransom or fine — [then in the case of] his fire as well, which is not subject to the law of ransom, let him pay [the victim's] monetary value [when it kills] unintentionally, since it is subject to the law of damages. However, [if he did so] intentionally, it is obvious to us that he is exempt [from paying], because he stands liable for the greater [penalty].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:8:1.english: There was a goat bound to it - To the stack [of grain].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:8:2.hebrew: חייב - אגדי ואגדיש, ופטור על העבד, דהיה לו לברוח:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:8:2.english: [He is] liable - For the goat and for the stack [of grain], and [he is] exempt regarding the slave, because he should have fled.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:8:3.hebrew: עבד כפות לו וגדי סמוך לו - ונשרפו עמו פטור. וקסבר רבא: האי פטור אעבד וגדי קאמר; אעבד — משום דאין תשלומין לעבד אלא במקום קנס, בשור המועד, ואגדי — משום דהיה לו לברוח. אבל משום דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה לא פטר ליה, דקסבר אשו משום ממונו ואין כאן חיוב מיתה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:8:3.english: A slave bound to it and a goat adjacent to it - and they were burned with it, he is exempt. And Rava holds [that] this [ruling of] "exempt" refers both to the slave and to the goat: for the slave, because there is no payment for [killing] a slave except in the case of a fine, with a mu'ad [forewarned] ox; and for the goat, because it should have fled. However, he does not exempt him on account of [the principle that] he incurs the greater [penalty], for he holds [that] one's fire is [categorized] as his property, and there is no liability for the death penalty here.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:9:1.english: Didn't Reish Lakish say - In the chapter [entitled] Keitzad.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:9:2.hebrew: כגון שהצית בגופו של עבד - דאיכא עליה חיוב מיתה, ואפילו אגדיש נמי פטר ליה משום דקם ליה בדרבה מיניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 43b:9:2.english: Where he ignited the body of the slave - For there is a death penalty liability upon him, and even for the stack of grain as well, [the Tanna] exempts him because he is subject to the greater [punishment] of them.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 43b:6:1.hebrew: אשו שלא בכוונה - על פי עדים לשלם דמים. כיון דשורו שלא בכוונה, אע"פ שאין יכול לבא בשום ענין לידי כופר וקנס, משלם דמים — אם כן באש נמי משלם דמים, אע"פ שאין יכול לבא בשום ענין לידי כופר. ולאו דוקא אשו שלא בכוונה, דכ"ש אשו בכוונה; דאי בכוונה פשיטא ליה דלא משלם דמים, היכי דייק מההוא דעבד כפות לו דפטור? דלמא ההיא בכוונה! ודוקא אליבא דמ"ד אשו משום ממונו פריך, דהויא דומיא דשור; אבל למ"ד אשו משום חציו — היינו אדם המזיק:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 43b:6:1.english: His fire unintentionally - based on [the testimony of] witnesses, [he is] to pay the value. Since [in the case of] his ox [killing] unintentionally, even though it cannot under any circumstances come to [liability for] ransom or a fine, he pays the value — if so, with fire as well, he pays the value, even though he cannot under any circumstances come to [liability for] ransom. And [it is] not specifically his fire unintentionally, for all the more so [is this true of] his fire intentionally; for if [regarding] intentionally it were obvious to him that he does not pay the value, how could he infer from that [case] of a slave bound before it that he is exempt? Perhaps that [case] was intentional! And he raises this difficulty specifically according to the one who says [that liability for] one's fire is because of his property, for it is comparable to an ox; but according to the one who says [that liability for] one's fire is because of his arrows, that is [equivalent to] a person who causes damage.
